hints: Look at the two cell types separately. What is the main job of red blood cells, and what is the main job of lymphocytes?

Think about when the body makes extra red blood cells (low oxygen availability) and when it makes extra lymphocytes (fighting infection with fever), and how extra oxygen delivery affects aerobic respiration.
walkthrough:
**Observe what has changed**

Both cell counts have gone up after one month. Red blood cells are higher and lymphocytes are higher. So we need one explanation for more oxygen transport and one for more immune activity.

**Explain the higher red blood cells**

Red blood cells carry oxygen. At higher altitude the partial pressure of oxygen is lower, so the body acclimatises by making more red blood cells to pick up enough oxygen.

More red blood cells also means more oxygen can be delivered to tissues, which can support a higher rate of aerobic respiration and so higher ATP synthesis.

**Explain the higher lymphocytes**

Lymphocytes are white blood cells involved in the immune response. A higher count suggests the person is fighting an infection.

Infection often causes fever, so body temperature is likely to be higher. Fever also raises metabolic rate, which further supports higher ATP synthesis.

**Put it all together**

Higher red blood cells fits moved to higher altitude and higher ATP synthesis. Higher lymphocytes fits higher body temperature and also higher ATP synthesis. All three statements can be true, which is option D.

options.A: This says no fever and no altitude move. That ignores the higher lymphocytes which suggest infection and fever, and the higher red blood cells which suggest acclimatisation to low oxygen.
options.B: This correctly includes higher altitude but wrongly says no fever and no extra ATP. Higher lymphocytes point to infection and fever, and extra oxygen delivery supports more aerobic respiration.
options.C: This correctly includes higher body temperature but wrongly says no altitude move and no extra ATP. Higher red blood cells point to higher altitude, which also allows more ATP synthesis.
options.D: This is correct. Higher lymphocytes suggest infection with fever, higher red blood cells suggest move to higher altitude, and both extra oxygen and fever support higher ATP synthesis.
